clue.text: Stage directors in groups

blocks.note: first meaning: the theatre, as in treading the planks of a stage
second meaning: company directors sit together in governing bodies

explanation.surface: Theatre directors gathering their actors into groups on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage directors' reads as one theatrical phrase, but the split falls after 'Stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors are said to tread the boards, meaning the theatre, and a company's directors collectively form its boards.

clue.text: Lois becomes a medium

definitions.note: the answer is plural in form but names one painting medium

indicators.note: to become something is to change form, so the name's letters are turned into something new

blocks.note: a girl's name, taken letter by letter

explanation.surface: A woman named Lois turns into a spiritualist who contacts the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, but here it is the artist's material.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil paint is one of the standard materials artists work in, alongside watercolour and acrylic.

clue.text: Critics about to join members of the audience

blocks.note: re is Latin-derived 'about, concerning'
people watching a show

explanation.surface: Theatre critics are about to take their seats among the ordinary audience.
explanation.definitionFit: People who write published assessments of plays, books or films are critics.

clue.text: Physical exercises I put off when on board

indicators.note: something gone off is spoiled or out of order, so the letters are rearranged
being on board a ship means being inside it, so letters go within the ship's abbreviation

blocks.note: a ship (steamship, SS) is what one is on board
taken as written

explanation.surface: A passenger postpones doing gym work while on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the convention for putting letters inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are a common floor exercise for strengthening the stomach muscles.

clue.text: Intrude by chance or mistake

indicators.note: a mistake puts things wrongly, so the letters come out in a jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone trespasses either accidentally or in error.
explanation.definitionFit: To encroach is to advance gradually onto another's territory or rights, which is trespassing.

clue.text: Prompt payments may be what archaeologists are looking for

blocks.note: first meaning: paying a bill or debt ahead of time
second meaning: the remains of an ancient village

explanation.surface: Paying bills on time might be what diggers are hunting for.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling an account before it is due, and an ancient community whose remains are excavated, both share this phrase.

clue.text: Carriage boy

blocks.note: first meaning: a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle
second meaning: a male first name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage boy' sounds like a footman or coach attendant; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence was a four-wheeled horse-drawn closed vehicle named after a Duke, and it is also a man's name.

clue.text: Deserted place of refreshment?

blocks.note: surface reading: an abandoned café or pub nobody visits any more
setter's reading: located in a desert, a fertile spot where travellers find water

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserted' normally means abandoned; here it means set in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot with water in a desert is where travellers and caravans stop to drink and rest.

clue.text: Old soldier who got the hump

definitions.text: Old soldier who got the hump

blocks.clueFragment: Old soldier who got the hump
blocks.note: surface reading: a grumpy veteran; 'got the hump' is British slang for sulking
setter's reading: the hump of the animal a desert trooper rode

explanation.walkthrough: 'Got the hump' is British slang for being in a bad mood, which hides the literal humped mount.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic military units mounted on dromedaries served in desert campaigns, so their troopers literally rode humps.

clue.text: Its users have no need to take flight to reveal confusion

definitions.text: Its users have no need to take flight

indicators.note: confusion is disorder, so the letters are thrown out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People who need not run away do so to expose some muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take flight' suggests fleeing, but means climbing a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift carries people between floors, so its passengers do not climb staircases.

clue.text: Put in on without being told?

definitions.note: probably a misprint for 'put it on', meaning to adopt or feign

blocks.note: first meaning: to put on or adopt, as an air or a manner
second meaning: to suppose something with no proof given

explanation.definitionFit: One can adopt a pose or disguise, and one can take a fact for granted without evidence; the verb covers both.

clue.text: They aren't charged, but make the most noise

definitions.text: They aren't charged, but make the most noise

blocks.clueFragment: They aren't charged, but make the most noise
blocks.note: surface reading: people let off by the police who nevertheless complain loudest
setter's reading: containers that are not filled, recalling a proverb about loud talkers

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says those with least to say talk the most, like hollow pots that clang loudly; 'charged' means filled, as with charged glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfilled containers ring loudly when struck, and the proverb applies this to foolish people who talk most.

clue.text: Oddly comic place associated with a criminal, perhaps

indicators.note: done oddly means done strangely, so the letters are set in an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A strange comedy venue turns out to be linked to a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take the odd letters of comic, but it is an anagram signal over both words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who helps another commit an offence is themselves guilty, so is an example of a lawbreaker.

clue.text: One outside hospital may need treatment

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so one word's letters go around the other

blocks.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards
H is the map-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A patient waiting outside the hospital might need medical help.
explanation.definitionFit: A persistent pain is something one may go to a doctor to have treated.

clue.text: Shellfish on edge

definitions.note: an ornamental border pattern on an edge

blocks.note: first meaning: a bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped shell
second meaning: a wavy decorative border cut along an edge

explanation.walkthrough: 'On edge' looks like nervousness; it means a curved pattern along a border.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an older spelling of scallop, both the mollusc and the curved border pattern copied from its shell.

clue.text: Idle girl going round giving choice to consumers

definitions.text: going round giving choice to consumers

blocks.note: idle means not working
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A lazy young woman wanders about offering shoppers a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving tray on a dining table lets diners turn it to choose dishes.

clue.text: It sounds highly unnatural

blocks.note: surface reading: something that seems very fake or implausible
setter's reading: a voice that produces high notes, artificially pitched above its normal range

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds' and 'highly' read as an idiom for seeming very; taken literally they describe a high-pitched voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A man singing above his natural range uses an artificial head voice, which is what this term names.

clue.text: Always faithful?

blocks.note: surface reading: a motto, like the Latin semper fidelis
setter's reading: unchanging over time, and also loyal

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both unvarying over time and steadfastly loyal, as in a lover.

clue.text: They are fast replacing buttons

blocks.note: surface reading: something quickly taking over from buttons
setter's reading: fasteners that hold clothing shut, and also quick

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast replacing' reads as 'quickly replacing', but 'fast' also means fastened shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothed sliding fasteners do the job buttons once did on clothes, and the word also means moves quickly.

clue.text: Quiet place for a school break

blocks.note: first meaning: a secluded nook or alcove
second meaning: playtime between lessons

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere peaceful during playtime.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove set back in a wall is secluded, and in American schools the mid-day playtime has this name.

clue.text: They restore plush to order

indicators.note: putting something to order arranges it afresh, so the letters are set out anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Craftsmen repair velvety furniture fabric on commission.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while two of its words supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradespeople who re-cover sofas and chairs with fabric such as velvet do exactly this work.

clue.text: Public minister raised in the Old Testament

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so letters run backwards
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, a clergyman
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A government minister brought up on the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open and done in plain view, rather than hidden, is the opposite of covert.

clue.text: It makes fast speed at sea

blocks.note: first meaning: a tie in rope that secures something
second meaning: one nautical mile per hour

explanation.surface: Something that makes a ship go quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes fast' suggests speeding up, but means ties securely.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie in a rope secures things, and the unit for a vessel's pace is one nautical mile per hour.

clue.text: Aim straight

blocks.note: first meaning: to point something at a target
second meaning: going without detours

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to shoot accurately; it is a verb and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means point at a target, and as an adjective it means without deviation or stops.

clue.text: Nevertheless, netting first and last service

indicators.note: first and last picks out only the two end letters of the word they follow

blocks.note: even so means nevertheless
the opening and closing letters of the word

explanation.surface: Despite everything, fishing nets come before a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Netting first' reads as catching something before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Anglican evening prayer service, sung in many cathedrals daily.

clue.text: Broken boot-tree found in the garden

definitions.note: a description of the answer rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces, which can be put back in a different order

blocks.note: a shoe-shaped form kept inside a boot; the hyphen is ignored

explanation.surface: A broken boot stretcher turns up among the flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: This red root vegetable is commonly grown in vegetable plots and allotments.

clue.text: One has no reason to want it

definitions.text: One has no reason to want it

blocks.clueFragment: One has no reason to want it
blocks.note: surface reading: there is no motive for desiring it
setter's reading: someone who has lost their mind lacks this soundness

explanation.walkthrough: 'No reason' reads as 'no motive'; it means having lost one's reason, so one lacks mental health.
explanation.definitionFit: Soundness of mind is what a person who has lost their reason is missing.
